However, I am getting error messages when I try to use it for the use case I had mentioned in that discussion. But at the very least the OpenAPI schema generation seems to indicate it should be supported.

query_text:
Would a PR adding tests for SSE (EventSourceResponse) with yield dependencies be welcome?

`test_dependency_after_yield_streaming.py` verifies that yield dependency cleanup runs correctly with `StreamingResponse`. There is no equivalent test for `EventSourceResponse` (SSE), which uses a different internal code path (`_sse_producer_cm` task group in `routing.py`).

I have written `tests/test_dependency_after_yield_sse.py` locally - 8 tests covering sync/async yield deps with SSE, cleanup verification, and broken dependency behaviour. All pass.

Would a PR adding this test file be welcome?

Example code:
```python
from collections.abc import Generator
from typing import Annotated, Any

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import EventSourceResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str

def dep_session() -> Any:
    # yield dependency - cleanup should run after stream ends
    yield [Item(name="foo"), Item(name="bar")]

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/sse", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
def sse_items(items: Annotated[list, Depends(dep_session)]) -> Any:
    def gen() -> Generator[Item, None, None]:
        yield from items

    return gen()
```
title: Would a PR adding tests for SSE (EventSourceResponse) with yield dependencies be welcome?
answer_text:
Glad the suggestions landed. Your call to skip the client-disconnect test is reasonable for the sync TestClient path, the race window really is too tight to assert anything meaningful. If you ever want to cover it later, the async route works: `httpx.AsyncClient` plus an explicit `aclose()` call mid-stream, then assert the cleanup sentinel ran exactly once. Lower priority though, the four tests you added cover the load-bearing cases.

Good luck with the PR. Happy to look at the diff if you open one.

query_text:
Enable Pydantic polymorphic_serialization flag on response serialization

* Pydantic 2.13+ uses `polymorphic_serialization=True` to serialize a model with its actual type vs declared type
    * PR: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12518
    * Release notes: https://pydantic.dev/articles/pydantic-v2-13-release
* When serializing a response it'd be great to either:
    * Be able to declare in the route to pass this flag when serializing (e.g., `@app.get(..., polymorphic_serialization=True)`), or...
    * For FastAPI to peek into the model's config to see if the flag is there, and if so apply it (this would be awesome!)

Example code:
```python
# this example is copied from the Pydantic docs with updates to work with FastAPI
# docs: https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/concepts/serialization/#polymorphic-serialization

from fastapi import FastAPI, Response
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

class User(BaseModel):
    name: str

class UserLogin(User):
    password: str

class OuterModel(BaseModel):
    # would love if FastAPI could read this!
    model_config = ConfigDict(polymorphic_serialization=True)

    user: User

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def current():
    model = OuterModel(
        user=UserLogin(name='pydantic', password='password'),
    )
    return model

@app.get("/expected")
def expected():
    model = OuterModel(
        user=UserLogin(name='pydantic', password='password'),
    )
    content = model.model_dump_json(polymorphic_serialization=True)
    return Response(media_type="application/json", content=content)
```
title: Enable Pydantic polymorphic_serialization flag on response serialization
answer_text:
I think all these flags that modify endpoint output making it different from what is declared in OpenAPI schema is bad idea and we shouldn't add more such flags.
There is already way to achieve this - by returning Response explicitly (as it's shown in the discussion)

how to upload file with None filename?

I checked the source code of UploadFile and found that filename can be None, 
but in fact fastapi/pydantic will report an error when receive a file without filename

https://github.com/eya46/httpx-file-test
```python
# clinet.py
import httpx, aiohttp

async def test_httpx(api: str):
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        resp = await client.post(
            api,
            files={
                "file": (None, b"test", "text/plain"),
            }
        )
        print("-" * 20)
        print("httpx", resp)
        print("httpx", resp.json())
        print("-" * 20)

async def test_httpx_default(api: str):
    """httpx set default filename to 'upload'"""
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        resp = await client.post(
            api,
            files={
                "file": b"test",
            }
        )
        print("-" * 20)
        print("httpx_default", resp)
        print("httpx_default", resp.json())
        print("-" * 20)

async def test_aiohttp(api: str):
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as client:
        resp = await client.post(
            api,
            data={
                "file": (None, b"test", "text/plain"),
            }
        )
        print("-" * 20)
        print("aiohttp", resp)
        print("aiohttp", await resp.json())
        print("-" * 20)

async def test_aiohttp_default(api: str):
    """aiohttp set default filename to 'file' ({key: file}, default filename = key)"""
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as client:
        resp = await client.post(
            api,
            data={
                "file": b"test",
            }
        )
        print("-" * 20)
        print("aiohttp_default", resp)
        print("aiohttp_default", await resp.json())
        print("-" * 20)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    from asyncio import run

    _api = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/uploadfile"
    run(test_httpx(_api))
    run(test_httpx_default(_api))
    run(test_aiohttp(_api))
    run(test_aiohttp_default(_api))

```

```python
app = FastAPI()

    data = file.file.read()

    uvicorn.run("server:app")
```

For anyone using FastAPI below `0.115.13`, please follow this section of the docs to redefine the ReDoc endpoint with a pinned version:


query_text:
Using scopes on `Security()` changes dependency inheritance

As you can see I have `scopes=["activate"]` defined in this `Security()` example.

The result will print:
```
get_authenticated_user: 140600933628496
user_activate: 140600933312848
```

As you can see the IDs of both sessions are different, this is unexpected to me as I was under the impression that arguments propagate through dependencies.

The weird thing is that when I remove `scopes=["activate"]` from `Security()` I do get the expected result:
```
get_authenticated_user: 139952151843088
user_activate: 139952151843088
```

I figured this out when I tried to commit a change in the `UserAccountInDatabase` object and sqlalchemy complained that the object does not belong to the same `Session`.

I'm wondering if this has anything to do with the instantiation of a SecurityScopes at some point by Security(). I tried manually adding the security scopes like this:
```python
activation_security_scope = SecurityScopes(["activate"])
@router.post('/activate', status_code=204)
async def user_activate(session: Session = Depends(get_session),
                        security_scopes: SecurityScopes = activation_security_scope,
                        user: UserAccountInDatabase = Depends(
                            get_authenticated_user)):
    print(f"user_activate: {id(session)}")
    print(security_scopes.scope_str)
```

But this actually will just show that `security_scopes` is empty, it almost seems like it's being overwritten somewhere (maybe by the `Depends(get_authenticated_user)`. 

As I'm new to FastAPI there's a big chance I'm misunderstanding something.

Example code:
```python
async def get_authenticated_user(security_scopes: SecurityScopes,
                                 session: Session = Depends(get_session),
                                 token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme),
                                 ):

    print(f"get_authenticated_user: {id(session)}")
    return

@router.post('/activate', status_code=204)
async def user_activate(session: Session = Depends(get_session),
                        user: UserAccountInDatabase = Security(
                            get_authenticated_user,
                            scopes=["activate"])):
    print(f"user_activate: {id(session)}")
    return
```
title: Using scopes on `Security()` changes dependency inheritance
answer_text:
[Dependant](https://github.com/tiangolo/fastapi/blob/63a5ffcf577abc6015d021f65857b3826d8db74e/fastapi/dependencies/models.py#L15) object has a cache_key attribute which the dependency resolver of fastapi uses it to cache dependencies and use the already resolved dependencies (get_session in this case).
according to [this line](https://github.com/tiangolo/fastapi/blob/63a5ffcf577abc6015d021f65857b3826d8db74e/fastapi/dependencies/models.py#L58) of Dependant class the cache_key is generated using the **dependency function reference** and **security scopes**.
when you use get_authenticated_user as a security dependency every param in get_authenticated_user gets the security scopes of the parent api (user_activate).
so when resloving dependencies from user_activate with scopes, the param ```session: Session = Depends(get_session)``` gets saved in dependency_cache with a key like ```(<function get_session at 0x7fb87827c9d0>, ('activate'))```
when resloving dependencies from user_activate with no scopes, the param ```session: Session = Depends(get_session)``` gets saved in dependency_cache with a key like ```(<function get_session at 0x7fb87827c9d0>, ())```

i think this behavior might be a security feature.

it might help you to read [this part of the doc](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies/sub-dependencies/?h=dependenc#using-the-same-dependency-multiple-times) on dependency cache
and [this part](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/security/oauth2-scopes/?h=dependency#dependency-tree-and-scopes) about dependency tree and scopes.

However, when I access the FastAPI endpoint, I'm receiving all the content at once (after the complete 5s needed to stream all content).

That is, when I access the endpoint with the following client code:
```python

import time
t0 = time.time()
response = requests.get('http://localhost:8080/test')
for chunk in response.iter_lines():
    print(f"Chunk (time {int((time.time()-t0)*1000)}ms): {chunk}")
```

That is, the chuncks of json content are being generated and yielded roughly every 500ms, but the client only see the the result at 5026ms.

If this is a problem with the client code (`requests` library), I apology for the misunderstanding.

Example code:

```python
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

import time

async def fake_json_streamer():
    t0 = time.time()
    for i in range(10):
        print(f"Chunk being yielded (time {int((time.time()-t0)*1000)}ms)", flush=True)
```

title: StreamingResponse is returning all content at once
answer_text:
hi @LeonardoSanBenitez  hope you have resolved the issue, i faced same issue currently and was able to solve it by using non asynchronous generator function, so in your case 

```
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

import json
import time
import asyncio

app = FastAPI()

def fake_json_streamer():
    t0 = time.time()
    for i in range(10):
        print(f"Chunk being yielded (time {int((time.time()-t0)*1000)}ms)", flush=True)
        yield json.dumps( {"message": "Hello World"}) + '\n'
        time.sleep(0.5)
    print(f"Over (time {int((time.time()-t0)*1000)}ms)", flush=True)

@app.get("/test")
async def test():
    return StreamingResponse(fake_json_streamer(), media_type='text/event-stream')
```

which worker for me, but don't have the clear explanation 
[this might be useful](https://stackoverflow.com/a/75760884)

Second, if you are executing a blocking operation (i.e., blocking I/O-bound or CPU-bound tasks) inside the [StreamingResponse](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/custom-response/#streamingresponse)'s generator function, you should define the generator function with def instead of async def, as, otherwise, the blocking operation, as well as the time.sleep() function that is used inside your generator, would block the event loop.

I have defined a POST request and have passed a string parameter. When I run this API using the Swagger/docs, and do not pass any value to the **status** field, it does not allow me to run the API since the status field is a mandatory field.

I tried using: 
status: str    -> Passed an empty value
status: str = Query(...)    -> Passed an empty value
status: str = Required.      -> Passed an empty value

How can an empty value be passed even if the parameter is a mandatory field?

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app.post("/test")
def get_data(status: str):
   return status
```

title: FastAPI accepting empty string value for a mandatory/required field
answer_text: @Nistha314e in Swagger UI there is an input for your query parameter and when calling 'execute' check if the input is empty, if is required, and if it's empty doesn't execute the function. But if you call the endpoint from an external request with another client it works if you don't set validation length because this 'http://localhost:8000/api/v1/test?status=' is simply a path with status equal to ''.

query_text:
Discriminated Unions Break When Wrapped in Annotated[Union, Body(...)] in FastAPI 0.124.1+

I'm experiencing a breaking change when upgrading from FastAPI 0.124.0 to
   0.124.1/0.124.2.

   What works:

     - FastAPI 0.124.0 - Both endpoint patterns work correctly
     - FastAPI 0.124.1+ - Only pet: Pet = Body(...) works

   What breaks:

     - FastAPI 0.124.1+ - The pattern pet: Annotated[Pet, Body(...)] fails
   with:

     pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `Tag` not provided for choice {
       'type': 'tagged-union',
       'choices': {
         'cat': {'type': 'definition-ref', 'metadata':
   {'pydantic_internal_union_tag_key': 'cat'}},
         'dog': {'type': 'definition-ref', 'metadata':
   {'pydantic_internal_union_tag_key': 'dog'}}
       },
       'discriminator': <function get_pet_type at 0x...>
     } used with `Discriminator`

     For further information visit
   https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.12/u/callable-discriminator-no-tag

   Root Cause: This appears to be caused by commit 42b250d (https://github.com
   /fastapi/fastapi/commit/42b250d14dd42d3c0c24dd085fa53878172a985f) which
   fixed arbitrary_types_allowed=True but introduced a regression in how
   discriminated unions are handled.

   The change in fastapi/_compat/v2.py now includes *self.field_info.metadata
   when creating TypeAdapters, which causes discriminator metadata to be
   duplicated/nested when the union is wrapped in Annotated[..., Body(...)].

   Workaround: Use pet: Pet = Body(...) instead of pet: Annotated[Pet,
   Body(...)]

Example code:
```python
from typing import Annotated, Union
from pydantic import BaseModel, Tag, Discriminator
from fastapi import FastAPI, Body

class Cat(BaseModel):
    pet_type: str = "cat"
    meows: int

class Dog(BaseModel):
    pet_type: str = "dog"
    barks: float

def get_pet_type(v):
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return v.get("pet_type", "")
    return getattr(v, "pet_type", "")

# Define discriminated union
Pet = Annotated[
    Union[
        Annotated[Cat, Tag("cat")],
        Annotated[Dog, Tag("dog")]
    ],
    Discriminator(get_pet_type)
]

app = FastAPI()

# ✅ THIS WORKS in 0.124.1+
@app.post("/pet/works")
async def create_pet_works(pet: Pet = Body(...)):
    return pet

# ❌ THIS BREAKS in 0.124.1+ (worked in 0.124.0)
@app.post("/pet/broken")
async def create_pet_broken(pet: Annotated[Pet, Body(...)]):
    return pet
```
title: Discriminated Unions Break When Wrapped in Annotated[Union, Body(...)] in FastAPI 0.124.1+
answer_text:
Thanks for the report! I created an issue here: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/14508

I'm looking at this now.

I fixed it here: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14512, it is now available in FastAPI 0.124.3 :tada:

answer_text:
The code example is outdated, but affter [this comment](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/4657#issuecomment-3123374081) I looked at this problem one more time and I got it.

The `openapi.json` endpoint implementation in code example is simplified compare to default implementation.
If you look at the default implementation of `openapi.json` endpoint, you will see that before calling `get_openapi` (it's inside `self.openapi()`) it updates `servers` by adding `url` equal to `root_path`.

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/d5d302c3da11262f4e320a9af5dbb9d13386e1b5/fastapi/applications.py#L999-L1011

The implementation shown in docs misses this part. It works well for apps that are mounted at `'/'`, but fails in other case.

So, to fix your problem you need to change the implementation of `/openapi.json` endpoint to something like:
```py
@private_subapp.get("/openapi.json")
async def openapi(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPBasicCredentials, Depends(security)],
    req: Request,
):
    # The following 3 lines may be moved to lifespan event
    app = cast(FastAPI, req.app)
    urls = (server_data.get("url") for server_data in app.servers)
    server_urls = {url for url in urls if url}

    root_path = req.scope.get("root_path", "").rstrip("/")
    if root_path not in server_urls:
        if root_path and app.root_path_in_servers:
            app.servers.insert(0, {"url": root_path})
            server_urls.add(root_path)

    return get_openapi(
        title=f"PRIVATE: OpenAPI",
        version="0.1.0",
        routes=private_subapp.routes,
        servers=app.servers,  # <- added
    )
```

OpenAPI schema: Missing description with Query parameters

* I would like to use classes with Fields with description for query parameters. Example:
   ```python
   class MyClass(BaseModel):
     bar: str = Field(description="This is Bar", alias="bar2")
   
   async def fct(data: MyClass = Depends()):
   ```
* The parsing works, aliases work. But the OpenAPI Schema does not show the description of the field.

To test
* Using the source code provided, go on http://localhost:8000/redocs
* Notice foo and bar2 are only described when used without `Depends()`. This is for a Body schema (using with refs in the OpenAPI JSON).
* The only way to have the description field is to use a `Query` structure as an argument *in* the init. The following also does not show the description.
   ```
   class MyClass(BaseModel):
     bar: str = Query(description="This is Bar", alias="bar2")
   ```

While this usage is not documented, I would be hoping to use Classes inheritance to define query parameters and reuse descriptions. This does not seem possible without adding it manually to the schema. Yet I was still unsure if it's an expected behavior since `alias` is still taken into account. The reason for using Fields would be to also re-use those schemas when returning a response.
Perhaps I am missing a Python feature that would make this possible when setting the `__init__` ? If I use `def __init__(self, xyz: B = Query()):`, I get `AssertionError: Param: xyz can only be a request body, using Body()` 

Thank you for your help

Example code:
```python

import uvicorn
from typing import List
from fastapi import Query
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
import os

class A(BaseModel):
    foo: str = Field(
        description="This is Foo",
    )

class B(A):
    bar: str = Field(
        description="This is Bar with alias",
        alias="bar2",
    )

class C(B):
    def __init__(self, xyz: str = Query(description="This is Xyz")):
        self.xyz = xyz

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url="/redocs")

rtr_api = APIRouter(prefix="/api")

@rtr_api.get(
    "/test1",
    description="Query me",
    summary="Querio-matic 1",
    response_model=List[B],
)
async def test(bdata: B = Depends()):
    return [bdata]

@rtr_api.get(
    "/test2",
    description="Query me 2",
    summary="Querio-matic 2",
    response_model=List[B],
)
async def test2(bdata: B):
    return [bdata]

@rtr_api.get(
    "/test3",
    description="Query me 3",
    summary="Querio-matic 3",
    response_model=List[C],
)
async def test3(bdata: C = Depends()):
    return [bdata]

app.include_router(rtr_api)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(
        app,
        port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8000")),
        host=os.environ.get("HOST", "localhost"),
        debug=True,
    )
```
title: OpenAPI schema: Missing description with Query parameters
answer_text:
Since FastAPI 0.115.0 you can oficially use Pydantic models to define Query parameters.
And descriptions work fine:

```python
from typing import List

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class A(BaseModel):
    foo: str = Field(description="This is Foo")

class B(A):
    bar: str = Field(
        description="This is Bar with alias",
        alias="bar2",
    )

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url="/redocs")

@app.get("/test1", response_model=List[B])
async def test(bdata: B = Query()):
    return [bdata]


@app.get("/test2", response_model=List[B])
async def test2(bdata: B):
    return [bdata]
```

query_text:
FastAPI segfaults with Python 3.14.0 on MacOS

* Create a new FastAPI environment e.g. with uv via the following
```
uv init .
echo "3.14.0" > .python-version
uv python install
uv add "fastapi[standard]"
```
* Run the example code via `uv run fastapi dev`.
FastAPI immediately segfaults:

```
❯ uv run fastapi dev --verbose
 ~/Programmieren/fastapi-segfault  main ?6                                                                  SEGV ✘  3.14.0    14:49:26
```

If I switch to Python 3.13, it works fine.

Demo repository can be found here: https://github.com/guerda/fastapi-segfaults

Example code:
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def read_root():
    return {"Hello": "World"}

@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
def read_item(item_id: int, q: str | None = None):
    return {"item_id": item_id, "q": q}
```
title: FastAPI segfaults with Python 3.14.0 on MacOS
answer_text:
Look at the path in your  faulthandler output:

```
/Users/philip/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14.0a6-macos-x86_64-none/lib/python3.14/...
```

That's not Python 3.14.0 final... it's **3.14.0 alpha 6** (`a6`). Even though your `.python-version` says `3.14.0` and `uv python install` ran without complaint, uv resolved to a stale alpha build it had cached from earlier in the 3.14 beta cycle, rather than downloading the actual final release. This is a known uv quirk. There are several open uv issues describing exactly this (astral-sh/uv#13361, #18414): a previously installed pre release CPython build gets reused/resolved instead of the version you asked for.

That fully explains the segfault. CPython alpha/beta builds are **not ABI-stable**... internal struct layouts can and do change between alpha6 and the final 3.14.0 release. `pydantic-core` (and friends like `uvloop`/`watchfiles`) ship compiled wheels built against the final 3.14 ABI. Load one of those into an alpha6 interpreter and you get a silent, traceback less SEGV - which is exactly what you saw, and exactly why it crashes deep inside `pydantic-core`'s class-creation code for `Secret` (that's the kind of code that touches CPython internals most directly).

**Fix:**

```bash
uv python list                      # confirm you have a stray cpython-3.14.0a6-... entry
uv python uninstall 3.14.0a6        # remove the alpha build
rm -rf .venv
uv python install 3.14.0            # explicit, full final version
uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.version)"   # confirm it says 3.14.0, NOT 3.14.0a6
uv sync
uv run fastapi dev
```

If `uv python list` still offers the alpha as the resolved match for `3.14.0`, that's a uv bug worth reporting on astral-sh/uv directly... but it isn't a FastAPI or Pydantic bug.

Peewee usage

**Description**

How can I use peewee ORM with fastapi?

**Additional context**

I'd love to use peewee rather than sqlalchemy for my API. However, all documentation seems to be oriented to SQLAlchemy. 

It seems like I can use peewee directly up to a certain point, however some stuff (like ForeignKey relations) don't really work by default.
title: Peewee usage
answer_text:
I just added support for Pydantic's ORM mode in FastAPI `0.30.0`. :tada: 

ORM mode is new, but it solves most of these cases. You can see the docs here: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/sql-databases/

The docs use examples with SQLAlchemy, but they should work equally for any other ORM. Actually, any object that has attributes (`item.name` instead of `item["name"`).

It also supports dynamic properties, hybrid attributes, relationships, lazy-loading, etc.

You declare the shape that you need to return in your Pydantic models with all the specific attributes and they take care of extracting the data from your ORM object.

Also, I'm now using quite a lot of Peewee recently for a project :man_shrugging: :grin: ...Although, I haven't integrated this yet, because I just released it 10 min ago :joy:

Async dependencies?

Hi there,

I have found synchronous dependencies very easy to deal with

```python
@lru_cache()
def get_client() -> Client:
  return Client( ... )

@app.get('/')
async def my_endpoint(client: Annotated[Client, Depends(get_client)]) -> dict[str, any] :
  data = await client.fetch()
  return data
```

But I have found asynchronous much more convoluted to deal with

This flat out doesn't work

```python
@lru_cache()
async def get_connection() -> Connection:
  client = await AsyncClient.connection( ... )
  return client

@app.get('/')
async def my_endpoint(client: Annotated[Connection, Depends(get_connection)]) -> dict[str, any] :
  data = await client.fetch() # AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'fetch'
  return data
```

You have to resort to an untyped storage on app state

```python
async def get_connection() -> Connection:
  client = await AsyncClient.connection( ... )
  return client

@app.startup()
async def setup_connection() -> Connection:
  app.state.connection = await get_connection()

@app.get('/')
async def my_endpoint(request: Request) -> dict[str, any] :
  connection: Connection = request.app.state.connection
  data = await client.fetch() 
  return data
```

Is there a well accepted general solution / standard procedure for dealing with async deps?
title: Async dependencies?
